Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask, and great to see legal looped in. Short summary up front: yes, we provide a documented CoC for tenant deletes in our Private/VPC offering and can supply both operational logs and a signed attestation. Below I outline the standard flow and options for accelerated timelines.

Summary flow (standard):
1) Customer requests tenant deletion via the Redwood Console or an authenticated API call.
2) Deletion job is queued and paired with an immutable job id.
3) Runtime stops accepting new requests for the tenant; KV cache and ephemeral artifacts are purged.
4) Snapshot and object-store deletion is initiated across configured regions.
5) Background purge jobs verify object-store tombstones and remove metadata indexes.
6) Deletion completion is recorded; logs and a deletion manifest (job id + checksums + timestamps) are generated and available for download.

Options for expedited wipe:
- Expedited erase: prioritized deletion window (SLA add-on) that targets completion within 24 hours from request.
- Cryptographic key retirement: for environments using customer-managed keys, we can immediately rotate/retire keys to render data unreadable while purge completes.

Evidence we can provide:
- Deletion manifest (job id, list of top-level blobs deleted, timestamps)
- Operational logs (deletion start/complete events)
- Snapshot lineage showing snapshot ids and deletion events
- Signed attestation (PDF) from Redwood security for enterprise customers

Im attaching our high-level erase playbook for reference and can follow up with karthik from Security to provide sample attestation language you can use in contract. Ben, looping you for pricing/sla notes. Marissa from CS will outline the ops checklist and handoff steps.

Best,

Hi Sanjay — outlining the operational checklist our on-call team follows when a tenant wipe is requested (for Private/VPC installs):

Operational checklist (customer-facing view):
- Verify authenticated request and authorization
- Lock tenant: signal runtime to reject new entry points
- Export final usage metrics and active KV snapshot for customer archive (if requested)
- Kickoff object-store deletion jobs across region(s)
- Verify snapshot removal and update snapshot lineage graph
- Run metadata index compaction and tombstone sweeper
- Confirm deletion manifest generation and sign-off with operations
- Deliver deletion manifest and optional signed attestation to the customer portal / SFTP / DocuSign link (per your preference)

Estimated timings (standard):
- Small tenant (<200GB): 24–72 hours
- Medium (200GB–2TB): 48–120 hours
- Large (>2TB) or cross-region replication: depends on backlog and retention windows; expedited SLA advised

Im attaching a machine-friendly CSV checklist we use during the handoff so legal/audit can reconcile events. Please tell me the preferred delivery method for artifacts (portal vs SFTP vs email + signed PDF).

Sanjay — Karthik from Security here. A few technical clarifications and a sample attestation paragraph you can paste into the contract: 

Technical clarifications:
- Snapshots: we maintain snapshot lineage in object metadata. When a snapshot delete is issued, the snapshot id is added to a deletion manifest and background workers remove underlying objects. We record deletion events to an immutable audit stream (append-only) that includes job id, worker id, region, and checksums.
- Backups: Redwood does not keep independent backups for customer-managed object stores unless specifically configured; if backups exist (by customer or partner services), we will coordinate the wipe and record the coordination in the manifest.
- Key retirement: For customer-managed keys (BYOK), cryptographic key retirement is the fastest way to render data inaccessible; prove-by-key-rotation can be included as evidence.

Sample attestation (editable):
"Redwood Inference, Inc. hereby certifies that, as of <completion_timestamp>, the tenant identified as <tenant_id> was removed from Redwood-managed compute and storage within the customer's Private/VPC environment. Deletion artifacts, including a deletion manifest (job id, list of top-level object identifiers, snapshot ids where applicable), operation logs, and checksums, were generated and retained for audit purposes for 90 days post-deletion. Copies of the manifest and the signed attestation will be delivered to the customer via the agreed delivery channel within 48 hours of completion."

If you want, I can produce a signed attestation (PDF) and a sample manifest for one of your non-prod tenants so Legal can review exact fields. Attached is a template we use for enterprise attestations.

-Karthik
